key_insight: A hierarchical planner combines local pose adjustment and global replanning to generate collision-free welding paths for non-standard workpieces with complex spatial seam layouts.
engineering_relevance: This enables more reliable offline programming for welding robots, reducing manual teach-in effort while improving safety and path quality in real shop-floor applications.
method: Extract weld seams from CAD models with OpenCASCADE and classify path nodes into primary endpoints and auxiliary safety points.
Use two-stage obstacle avoidance: local attitude adjustment for short approach/retreat segments and global replanning for long transition segments.
Apply vanilla ABIT* with a distance-dependent three-stage adaptive objective to balance guidance, obstacle clearance, and goal convergence.
evidence_signal: On typical box-type workpieces, the method reduced average path length by 20%, increased minimum clearance by 8%, and improved practical success rate from 52% to 90.7% with retries.
watch_item: Performance depends on accurate CAD seam extraction and careful tuning of the staged objective and replanning logic for different workpiece geometries.
paper_title: A hierarchical collision free path planning method for multi line spatial distributed welding of non standard workpieces
